version.changelog:
# talkies 1.3.3

- Added explicit `permissions` section to clarify security, HTTP, shell usage, and file operations.
- Updated documentation to include important legal/ethical notice for Qwen3-TTS voice cloning; links to extended setup guidance.
- Minor clarifications to server-side URL fetching and voice usage.
- Removed the obsolete `skill-card.md` file.

llm.summary: This skill connects to a user-configured speech server, and its media upload, voice cloning, and persistence risks are clearly disclosed with guardrails.

dimensions.detail: Network and shell use are proportionate for a self-hosted speech API, but users must point TALKIES_URL only at trusted servers and avoid exposing unauthenticated instances.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Setup uses documented Docker images, bind-mounted data storage, and model downloads; this is substantial but disclosed and configurable with model whitelisting, auth, and loopback binding examples.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill gives explicit limits for administrative unload/delete actions, staged-file access, server-side URL fetching, and voice cloning consent; it does not instruct hidden or automatic use outside user workflows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Server-side staged files and URL downloads persist until deletion and are not per-caller isolated, but the artifact prominently discloses this and instructs agents to clean up only their own staged files.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose is a self-hosted ASR/TTS service, and the documented HTTP, Docker, curl, ffmpeg, staged-file, MCP, and voice-cloning capabilities all fit that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to run or trust the talkies server. Enable TALKIES_AUTH_TOKEN for any shared or exposed deployment, bind to loopback or a protected network, avoid sending private media URLs unless the server is trusted, clean up staged files after use, and use voice cloning only with authorization and speaker consent.
llm.findings:
[LP4] expected: The declared network permission is matched by documented calls to the configured TALKIES_URL and by the server-side URL download feature, so it is not unsupported staging.
[E1] expected: The curl examples send audio or text to the configured speech server as the core service behavior; the artifact repeatedly warns that the destination must be trusted and access-controlled.
[EA2] expected: The cited consent language is an acceptable-use warning for voice cloning, not an instruction to act autonomously or impersonate anyone.
[TM1] expected: The DELETE and unload endpoints are documented resource-management operations with explicit guardrails requiring user-directed administrative or cleanup intent.
